/ Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] / life in the Church. /
Although all the sects of the world may make offerings of alms in the name of God, it is only the holy church of the elect that can purify the light. Thus the elect are the only means for its release; and they themselves depend wholly upon the catechumens, who give the alms.
Mani compares the catechumens to good earth in which the good tree of the elect can grow. Similarly, the living soul can only ascend to rest through the sun and the moon, and again these light-givers will only rest in the land of light. So, too, both the elect and the catechumens will finally find rest in the land of light.
